HSTU already supports the proposed mechanism: its 2024 formulation adds learned relative positional and temporal bias to attention scores before SiLU weighting, retaining gated aggregation rather than softmax attention. Thus, adding timestamp-gap buckets to a positional-only baseline preserves the HSTU family. Temporal bias can distinguish interactions equally distant in sequence position but separated by different elapsed times; it does not inherently enforce monotonic decay. [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3). Follow-up experiments in *Scaling New Frontiers* explicitly compare position-only, time-only, combined bias and RoPE, reporting stronger HR/NDCG with temporal information than position alone in their settings. [Ablation study](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=e6pqwHR1Yh).

Related work supports adaptive temporal weighting without assuming recent always means relevant. The 2025 *Long-Term Interest Clock* uses time-gap-aware attention to recover relevant long-term behaviors; the 2026 HyTRec preprint emphasizes fresh signals while suppressing historical noise, although its hybrid backbone should not replace HSTU here. [LIC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15817), [HyTRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.18283). Conversely, a 2024 study reports excessive recency bias can harm recommendation accuracy. [Recency-bias study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722).

Experiment implication: compare positional-only against jointly learned position-plus-time bias within one HSTU per category. Use observed historical timestamps only; exclude unavailable target-time gaps. Timestamp shuffling with item order fixed, recent/older-context removal, and gap-stratified sensitivity are useful proposed in-sample diagnostics, not evidence of latent user traits or validation gains. Select using the host’s macro validation HR@10; these papers do not establish improvements on the four pinned Amazon datasets.
